chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ismail. He said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the egg of the crow, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat it'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating crow eggs in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam al-Rida’s (peace be upon him) specific ruling on the permissibility of consuming crow eggs, which he explicitly prohibited. This ruling is often discussed within the context of *kharjin* (dung-eating birds) and their eggs, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential approach to distinguishing between general avian permissibility and specific exclusions based on the Prophet's and Imams' traditions. The narration highlights the detailed nature of dietary laws in Shia fiqh, where even specific parts of otherwise permissible animals can be subject to prohibition or strong dislike (*makruh*).
